meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He wrote it somewhere else and pasted it in, kids do that. Did you speak to Owen before you entered that mark?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and nobody in his class hears a word. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
I'm reading it. A wrong act and scene is a seventeen-year-old's citation error, Hale. Is that line anywhere in the play?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. So what are you asking for?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Two weeks between an outline and an essay; students change their minds, that's the point of an outline. And I asked what you're asking for.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
He'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him and for no other reason. I'll want your email tonight, with nothing on his record in the first line. That you never spoke to Owen first goes in mine.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday, November 12. I'll confirm it with Owen tonight. Put the time and the room in your email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,
cc: Principal

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite for Owen under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday, November 12, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require your written confirmation of those terms, with nothing on his record stated in the first line and the time and room included, and a direct answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered on November 3. You said I would have this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, to put this behind him and for no other reason. She still wants your written confirmation tonight with the promise about his record first, the time and room, and an answer on whether Owen was heard before the zero. This is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its times, and when she said he pasted it in from somewhere else, you invited the dated draft instead of arguing. It was a dated record she could check, and her one defence had an answer.
What cost ground: you never answered whether you spoke to Owen before entering the mark, though she asked twice. It cost you no position, but it left her a procedural point to put in front of the principal.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence came very close, since your version history put the whole essay arriving between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, a late night in October. That proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked the second time whether you spoke to Owen before entering the mark, answer it in one plain sentence before you move on to the draft.
